description: In a combinatorial auction, agents bid on whole bundles of tasks, so they can say that tasks are worth more together. `bundle_bids` lists an agent's most valuable bundles up to a size, each valued by its best build order, and an agent wins at most one of its bids (*XOR bids*). `winner_determination` then picks at most one bundle per agent, with no task in two of them, that maximizes the total value; it is exact, a depth-first branch and bound over agents pruned by each remaining agent's best bid. The problem is NP-hard and the search grows with the number of bids, so plan for a few dozen; with enough bids per agent, `combinatorial` finds the optimal assignment. Like the sequential auction it needs a central auctioneer; use it when synergies between tasks matter and the instance is small, and CBBA when there is no auctioneer.

papers.title: Algorithm for optimal winner determination in combinatorial auctions
